text:
sqlpipe has three components: a reader, a converter, and an uploader. Each component runs in a separate process. They communicate through buffered queues.

The reader connects to Postgres and streams rows in fixed-size batches. It does not load the full table into memory. When a batch is full, the reader sends it to the converter.

The converter takes each batch and maps Postgres column types to Parquet types. Then it writes the batch as a Parquet row group. When the row group is complete, the converter sends it to the uploader.

The uploader writes each row group to S3 as a multipart object. If a part fails, the uploader retries that part. The uploader does not restart the full upload. When all parts are uploaded, S3 assembles them into one object.
